results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what they've been played with.

Bringer of the Last Gift and Superior Spider-Man are legal, but neither appears in any list in the results. Town Greeter is mainly in Golgari Roots. Next I'll look at the Standard field and the Golgari Roots and Rogue shells.

The Golgari Roots list is the best donor shell: it already runs Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk, and graveyard fuel. Before I pick a direction, I'll check the mill, reanimation, and ramp cards that would support Bringer and Spider-Man in Standard.

Two of the Golgari cards are not legal in Standard: Tyvar and Scrapwork Mutt. That changes the shell. Next I'll check the ramp, removal, and mill creatures available in black-green, and the blue cards that would support Spider-Man.

The pool supports a Golgari graveyard shell with a light blue splash. I'll confirm the dual lands and the removal and finishers I'm considering.

I have enough to build. Llanowar Wastes and Go for the Throat are not legal in Standard, so I'll leave them out. Next I'll check the deck's mana and legality, and confirm the sideboard candidates.

The deck passes check_deck with no errors or warnings. Its mana (14 green, 14 black, 8 blue sources) is close to the Golgari shell's, and the blue is limited to splashing Spider-Man. I'll submit it as a brew built on the Golgari Roots shell.

The checker flagged four removal spells as rarely played. Each one answers a specific threat in this deck, so I'll keep them and say why.

I submitted a Golgari graveyard deck built around Bringer and Superior Spider-Man, with a light blue splash for Spider-Man. Of the three directions I weighed, I chose this one because Golgari Roots is the only shell that supplies both the graveyard fuel and the mana for an 8-drop. A Dimir version has Spider-Man's colors but almost no ramp, and a mono-black reanimation version lacks mana and still needs the blue splash.

The plan is to mill creatures early with Town Greeter and Overlord of the Balemurk, copy the best milled creature with Spider-Man on turn 4, and cast Bringer around turn 8. The honest caveat is that the Bringer line is slow: the checker estimates the full line is drawn by turn 8 in only about 3.4% of games. Spider-Man is the early engine, and Bringer is a late-game finisher that works best when both graveyards hold creatures worth returning.

Llanowar Wastes, Tyvar and Go for the Throat are not legal in Standard, so I left them out. The checker flagged four removal spells as rarely played; I kept them because each answers a specific threat the deck needs answered before turn 8.

Turn 2: mills four, fills the graveyard with creatures and puts a land in hand.

Turn 8: cast it for 8 (Elves, Molt Tender, lands); each player sacrifices other creatures, then creature cards that died earlier return from both graveyards, leaving a 6/6 flier on board.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:

Mightform Harmonizer is green, Full Bore is red, Spell Snare is blue, and no published list runs all three. Next I'll check the individual cards' partners and the Landfall and warp options.

The three requested cards don't share a color: Harmonizer is green, Full Bore is red, Spell Snare is blue. Before choosing a direction, I'll check the Landfall package from the menu and the warp options in red and green.

The Landfall shell is a green base with Tifa, Chocobos, Bristly Bill, Mossborn Hydra and Llanowar Elves. Next I'll verify the exact text and cost of the cards I'm considering for the red and blue pieces.

Lightning Strike, Burst Lightning and Scorching Dragonfire are common in the meta, and several of them cost two mana, so Spell Snare has real targets. Next I'll check the sideboard candidates from the Landfall list.

Harmonizer and Full Bore together by turn 4 is about 27% on the play, so the line is real but not reliable. I'll check the full draft with the Landfall mana as the comparison.

The checker says 17 lands is too few for a landfall deck (Landfall lists run about 25 land-like cards), so I'll move to 19 lands and trim two low-impact creatures to keep 60 cards.

The deck passes the checker: no errors, and the only warning is land count, which I'm keeping at 19 because the four Llanowar Elves bring total mana sources to 23. I'll submit it.

I built a Gruul-style Landfall deck with a blue splash for Spell Snare, submitted as a brew. It's built around a turn-4 line: warp Mightform Harmonizer for {2}{G}, cast Full Bore on it (+3/+2, plus trample and haste because it was warped), then play a land so the landfall trigger doubles its power from 7 to 14. That is 14 hasty trample damage for four mana. The order matters: Full Bore has to resolve before the land drop.

I picked this direction over two others. An Izzet build would keep Spell Snare and Full Bore but drop Harmonizer, and a Boros build would keep Full Bore but drop both others. The green Landfall core is the only one that keeps the Harmonizer line.

The deck runs 19 lands plus four Llanowar Elves, which the checker still flags as light; I kept 19 because landfall needs land drops. The line lands on turn 4 only about 27% of the time on the play, so it's a real plan but not a reliable one. Spell Snare (two copies) is there to counter the two-mana removal that would kill Harmonizer, such as Lightning Strike and Abrade.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a brew: a green-white airbend midrange build with 20 lands, 8 mana creatures, and the 15-card sideboard. Check_deck passed with no errors or warnings.

**Plan:** Ramp on Llanowar Elves and Bramble Familiar, then use Innkeeper's Talent and Ouroboroid to grow the board. Appa flashes in to airbend Ouroboroid, and you recast it for {2} with a 1/1 Ally token, while Elspeth doubles tokens and pumps the team for the finish. Get Lost, Parting Gust and Airbender's Reversal handle the early threats. The win line is turn 6.

**Direction:** I weighed three options. (1) Green-white, borrowing the Selesnya Offense core, which I chose because it gives Appa's WW and Airbender Ascension a real white base. (2) Temur Rogue, which already plays Appa but has no white, so Ascension would need a splash. (3) Blue-white Aang control, which drops Bramble Familiar and the ramp plan.

**Caveats:** No real list runs this exact combination, so the shell is borrowed and the airbend package is untested. Aang, the Last Airbender and Airbending Lesson have no results in the last 30 days. I kept 20 lands, below the tool's 22.8 recommendation, because eight mana creatures supply the rest. I left the Selesnya Offense mana base alone except for the green-white duals.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:

Only one recent list runs these three cards, and it is Mono-Red. Next I'll pull that list, the Izzet Aggro shell (a red package from the menu), and the Lesson cards in Standard.

The Lesson package is mostly red, so the core question is which red shell to build around. I'll check the Lesson-type cards in red and blue and get exact text for the candidate creatures and burn.

Screaming Nemesis shows as **banned** in Standard, so the Izzet and Boros lists that run it are out of date. I'll keep it out. Next I'll check the red removal and the red creatures that fit a Lesson deck.

I have enough to choose a direction. Three options:

1. **Mono-Red Lessons.** Start from the one list that runs the three cards, and add the red core of Izzet Aggro (Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut, Razorkin Needlehead, Nova Hellkite, burn). Every card the request names is red or colorless, so the mana is clean.
2. **Izzet Lessons.** Use the full Izzet Aggro shell and add blue Lessons. The blue Lessons available (Accumulate Wisdom, Boomerang Basics, It'll Quench Ya!) are weak, so this adds mana strain for little gain.
3. **Boros Lessons.** Use Boros Aggro with Aang and Master Piandao. Both are white and need a second color for little density.

I'm going with option 1. It keeps all three requested cards at full strength and gives the most Lessons per card slot. I'm checking the draft now.

The checker flags 18 lands against a very low curve (average mana value 1.9). The proven Mono-Red list runs 20, and the deck has several mana sinks (Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut, the kickers). I'll move to 19 lands and cut Iroh's Demonstration, the weakest spell, to make room.

The checker is clean now. Before I submit, I need exact text for the sideboard card I haven't looked up yet (Sunspine Lynx). I'll also check the odds of finding a Lesson early.

Everything checks out. Submitting the deck with a 15-card red sideboard aimed at the field.

The deck is submitted as a brew. It's a mono-red Lessons deck built on the one recent list that runs your three cards (Mono-Red, 13th at Standard Challenge 32), with the red core of Izzet Aggro swapped in: Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut, Razorkin Needlehead, Nova Hellkite, Burst Lightning and Lightning Strike.

**Direction:** I went mono-red over Izzet or Boros because all three of your cards are red or colorless, and blue or white would add only weak Lessons or cost mana consistency. The plan is to curve out with cheap creatures, use Abandon Attachments to loot away extra lands and fill the graveyard with Lessons, then use Combustion Technique and Firebending Lesson to clear blockers. Nova Hellkite and burn finish the game, with a target of turn 5.

**Things to know:**
- Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so the Izzet and Boros lists in the menu that run it are out of date. I left it out.
- The Mono-Red evidence is one list, and the field share is only 0.2%, so the deck is a sound build rather than a proven one.
- The checker wanted 22 lands for this low curve. I ran 19 (18 Mountain, Fire Nation Palace) because the deck has several mana sinks, including Hired Claw, Burnout Bashtronaut and the kickers.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
**Deck: U/R all-Elemental midrange built around Ashling and Sunderflock (brew, submitted and accepted with no check warnings).**

I considered three directions: a Rogue-style U/R list (Rogue plays Sunderflock, but mostly with non-Elementals that its bounce hits), a Simic Ouroboroid list with Bounce Off (drops Ashling and Sunderflock), and an all-Elemental U/R build. I chose the last because all 24 creatures are Elementals, so Sunderflock's "return all non-Elemental creatures" only hits the opponent's board. The mana base and burn come from Izzet Aggro, the most-played U/R list.

**The plan:** Ashling on turn 2, then pay U to flip it into Rimebound, which adds 2 mana for 4+ drops each turn. That turns into Shinestriker or Eddymurk Crab, which make Sunderflock cost about 3 mana. Sunderflock then wipes the opponent's non-Elemental creatures and leaves a 5/5 flyer. Flamebraider's 2 mana and cheap burn cover the early turns.

**Honest odds:** Ashling by turn 5 on the play is about 57%, and Sunderflock by turn 5 is about 46%. Having both Ashling and a Sunderflock cost-reducer by turn 5 is only about 13%. The exact written win line has been drawn by turn 5 in only about 1.4% of games, so expect the deck to win mostly through its Elemental board and burn, with Sunderflock as the late-game swing.

winLine.does: Turn 2 cast; turn 3 pay U at first main to transform into Rimebound, which adds 2 mana usable on MV 4+ spells.
Turn 3 or 4: 4-drop flyer cast with Rimebound mana plus lands, adds board presence.
Turn 4: cast with 4 lands plus Rimebound's 2 mana; a 6-MV Elemental that makes Sunderflock cost {1}{U}{U}.
Turn 5: cast for about 3 mana; its ETB returns all opposing non-Elemental creatures to hand while our Elementals stay, then the 5/5 flyer attacks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.
results.text:
I submitted a mono-black brew built on Doomsday Excruciator, Archenemy's Charm and Insatiable Avarice, borrowing the Mono-Black shell from a recent 5-0 league list (black lands, Bitter Triumph, Deep-Cavern Bat, Preacher of the Schism, Qarsi Revenant). I considered three directions: mono-black, Dimir Midrange (Excruciator's current home, but it splits black with blue and makes six black pips hard), and Rogue (Avarice's home, but no list in the menu to borrow from). I chose mono-black because Excruciator's BBBBBB and the Charm's BBB need almost every land to make black.

The plan is to land Bloodletter of Aclazotz on turn 4, then cast Excruciator around turns 7–9 and attack. Bloodletter doubles the opponent's life loss on my turn, so one Excruciator hit deals 12 and the flyers finish it in about two swings. Excruciator's mill also thins both libraries to six cards, so my own decking clock is real: I have roughly three turns of attacks after it lands. The tool estimates the full line is in hand by turn 9 in only about 18% of games, so this is a slow, grindy deck that wins on removal and card advantage first. The deck passed check_deck with no errors or warnings, and the 15-card sideboard is aimed at the Landfall, Simic Ouroboroid and aggro decks on the menu.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a brew: a Jeskai Control shell with a light black splash for Inevitable Defeat. Resonating Lute and Jeskai Revelation sit at the center. Lute doubles your lands' mana for instants and sorceries, which makes Revelation (7 mana) castable on turns 5 to 6. Elspeth, Storm Slayer closes the game once the board is stable.

I chose this direction over two others. A Rogue or Mardu build around Inevitable Defeat has the most support (27 Rogue lists run it), but none of them play Lute or Revelation. A pure Azorius Lute-control build would have needed red and black removal anyway, so it fit worse. Jeskai was the only shell where both named cards are on-color and the removal suite is already proven.

Be aware of two weak points. Inevitable Defeat is only about 63% likely to have a black source by turn 7 with four black sources, so it will sometimes sit in hand. The turn-6 win line is also unlikely as a full sequence: the tool reports only about 1% of games have every card in it drawn by then. Treat it as a midgame control deck that wins through card advantage and Elspeth, not a fast combo.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
I submitted a 60-card RW Dwarves-and-Equipment brew. It borrows Boros Aggro's mana base and burn, since no published list runs these three cards together. It was accepted, with one warning: 16 lands against a low curve (average mana value 2.11, 10 one-drops), which is below the 23 the checker's heuristic suggests. I kept 16 because the deck is built to spend early mana, but it is untested.

**Directions considered:**
1. **RW Dwarves + Equipment (chosen):** Dáin's Company and Kíli need white, and the Boros lands and burn support that. Dwarves and Equipment feed Kíli's draw and Dáin's Company's dig.
2. **Mostly red Dwarves with red equipment:** Chainsaw, Mjölnir, and Samurai's Katana work, but Dáin's Company and Kíli lose their color.
3. **White Dwarves with white equipment:** Paladin's Arms and Dragoon's Lance are weaker than the red removal-equipment, so this has less power.

**The plan:** Turn 1 Dwarven Mauler, turn 2 Kíli or Dáin's Company, then Stalactite Dagger on turn 3. The Dagger's changeling token counts as a Dwarf, so Dáin's Company gains lifelink, and Kíli draws off the Dagger entering. From there, equipment like Lost Jitte and Samurai's Katana goes on the board, Thorin, Mountain-king clears a blocker, and burn finishes.

The deck has 24 Dwarves, 11 Equipment, 8 burn spells and 16 lands. Chainsaw and Shock were flagged as rarely played; I kept both and explained why in the submission. Chainsaw's ETB damage also triggers Kíli, and Stockpiling Celebrant can bounce it to fire again.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.

I have what I need for the sideboard. I'll run the full check with the 15-card sideboard before submitting.

I considered three directions: mono-black sacrifice, a Dimir build borrowing the Dimir Midrange package, and a Mardu build borrowing the Mardu Discard package. The plan is to start with cheap fodder (Freebooter, Infestation Sage, Common Crook, Undercity Dire Rat, Treasure Dredger), turn each sacrifice into a Treasure or a card through Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot, and then land a 6-drop finisher: Vein Ripper drains 2 for every creature that dies, and Liliana, Dreadhorde General draws off deaths. The honest caveat is that the line is slow and fragile: the tool estimates it is fully drawn by turn 6 in only 2.7% of games. The deck has no published list to copy, so treat it as an experiment; the Mono-Black results it borrows its mana from are a different, non-sacrifice build.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Sentinel of the Nameless City, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder.

Sentinel, Abrupt Decay and Tear Asunder are at the center: Sentinel is the turn-3 threat, Decay and Tear Asunder handle early threats and anything else, and Garruk and Vraska close games. Recent results show no list running these three together, so this is a brew, not a proven list.

results.prompt: Brew me a Vintage deck built around Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam.
results.text:
I built a blue-red Goblin Welder combo deck with a Lurrus Control counter suite. It's accepted as a brew, with 14 lands and 8 mana rocks, and a sideboard of 15.

**Plan:** Goblin Welder swaps Sewer-veillance Cam and Legion Extruder between the battlefield and graveyard each turn. Cam's enter and leave triggers untap Welder, so the swap loops, and every Extruder entry deals 2 to the opponent. Goblin Engineer puts Extruder into the graveyard to start it, and Force of Will, Force of Negation, Spell Pierce, Mental Misstep and Gitaxian Probe protect the setup. Ancestral, Brainstorm, Reshape and Trash for Treasure help find the pieces.

**Direction chosen:** I considered three. (1) Blue-red Welder combo with the Lurrus Control counter package, which I picked. (2) A red-only Legacy-style Sewer build, which drops Cam, the blue piece that makes the loop work. (3) A Raker or Sphere Shops artifact shell with Welder as a side engine, which lacks Cam and Extruder. I went with (1) because all three requested cards are needed and the counters protect a combo that wins with only 3–4 pieces.

**Honest odds:** The turn-2 nut needs Welder, Cam, Engineer and a mana source in the opening hand. Each of Welder, Cam and Engineer is about 44–49% to appear by turn 2–3, but all four core pieces together are only 3.7% by turn 3 on the play with no mulligans. The cantrips and Reshape/Trash raise that, but I didn't compute a higher figure. Expect the combo to come online by turn 3–4 more often than turn 2.

**Sources:** The Sewer combo shape comes from a Legacy list (2 results), not a Vintage list, so this is a Vintage adaptation. The counter package is borrowed from Lurrus Control (388 lists in the last 30 days). Prophetic Prism was flagged as rarely played; I kept it because Welder can rebuy it for another card.
